title: Manage quantity and quality of resources (resources include but are not limited to water supply system and holding facilities, feed, air, consumables, equipment; equipment and facilities include but are not limited to: screens, nets, baskets, tanks, pipe work, plumbing, etc.)

lessons.title: Managing water supply, air and holding facilities
lessons.html:
The supervisor's daily resource check

In this practical module you take responsibility for keeping resources at the right quantity and quality. Start each shift with a structured walk-through of the water supply, aeration and holding units, and record what you find.

Water supply system

  • Check source levels: borehole pump running, dam or reservoir level, header tank full.
  • Check flow into each unit; compare with the target flow on the unit card. Measure flow with a bucket and stopwatch if there is no meter: litres collected divided by seconds.
  • Inspect pipework, valves, joints and plumbing for leaks, air locks and blockages.
  • Check inlet and outlet screens: clean, intact, correctly seated. A blocked outlet screen can overflow a tank; a damaged one lets fish escape.

Air and oxygen

  • Confirm aerators, blowers and diffusers are running and evenly bubbling.
  • Check oxygen supply pressure and cylinder or tank levels where pure oxygen is used.
  • Take dissolved oxygen and temperature readings at the set times and compare with target ranges.
  • Confirm alarms and standby generator are ready; check fuel level.

Holding facilities

  • Tanks, raceways and ponds: water level correct, walls and liners intact, no cracks or leaks.
  • Covers and bird nets in place.
  • Waste removed: siphon solids, flush standpipes, clean sumps as scheduled.
  • Stocking density within plan; flag units that need splitting.

Acting on what you find

Rank problems: anything threatening fish life now (low oxygen, no flow, power failure) is handled immediately using the emergency procedure; leaks and minor damage are logged and scheduled; recurring faults are reported for repair or replacement. Isolate and lock out power before working on pumps or aerators, and never work alone in deep ponds.

Record readings, faults and actions on the daily resource sheet, signed with the time.

lessons.title: Managing feed, consumables and equipment
lessons.html:
Feed

  • Quantity: keep stock between the minimum and reorder level. Calculate daily use from the feeding plan and place orders in time for the supplier's lead time.
  • Quality: on delivery check bag condition, labels, pellet size, batch and manufacture or expiry dates. Reject wet, torn, mouldy or heated bags.
  • Storage: on pallets, off walls, dry, shaded, ventilated, rodent- and bird-proof. Issue first in, first out.
  • Use: weigh feed per unit from the feeding chart; observe feeding response and adjust; record feed given and any waste.

Consumables

Includes salt, lime, disinfectants, remedies, test kit reagents, fuel, ice, packaging and protective equipment. Keep a stock card for each, with receipts, issues and balance. Store chemicals locked, labelled and separate from feed, with safety data sheets available. Check expiry dates; expired reagents give false readings.

Equipment and facilities

ItemCheck
Nets and seinesHoles, frayed edges, correct mesh size, clean and dry after use
Baskets, crates, gradersCracks, sharp edges that damage fish, disinfected between units
Tanks and linersLeaks, algae build-up, damaged fittings
Pipework and plumbingLeaks, blockages, valve operation
Scales and metersCalibration and battery

Keep equipment allocated per unit or section, and use colour coding to stop nets moving between quarantine and production areas.

Quality control loop

  1. Set standards (target ranges, stock levels, condition criteria).
  2. Measure and inspect against them.
  3. Correct deviations and record actions.
  4. Review weekly and improve the system.

Your assessor will expect to see completed records, correct calculations and safe practice.

Key points

  • Check water flow, levels, screens and pipework every shift.
  • Confirm aeration, oxygen supply, alarms and generator readiness.
  • Inspect feed on delivery and store it dry, off the floor, first in, first out.
  • Keep stock cards for feed and consumables; check expiry dates.
  • Maintain and disinfect nets, crates and tanks; record faults and repairs.
